candidates.explanation: When a social login matches an existing user by email (and no user is found by socialId), the code overwrites provider and socialId on the existing account whenever its status is not inactive. So an active email/password user gets hijacked: provider becomes 'google', and validateLogin then rejects email login because user.provider !== email. The check is inverted/wrong: it relinks active accounts (and skips inactive ones). It should not change the provider of an active password account (e.g. reject, or only link without changing provider).

fix.description: In the `else if (userByEmail)` branch, do not overwrite provider/socialId on an existing active account. Either throw an UnprocessableEntityException (e.g. email: 'emailAlreadyExistsWithProvider') when the existing user's provider is email and status is active, or just log in without modifying provider/password. Only link social identity in a way that keeps provider as 'email', e.g. store socialId separately, or after explicit verification.
